quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

37 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: The most important thing about managing speed on curves is to:

options.text: Drive at the posted speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Accelerate gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the posted speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle's momentum makes it harder to turn. Slow down before entering a curve to keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When driving 45 mph or faster, signal to turn ____ before you start the turn.
questions.explanation: Signal at least 200 feet before you turn or change lanes when driving faster than 45 mph. This tells other drivers what you plan to do. Keep signaling until you finish the turn or lane change.

questions.question: In normal weather and traffic, keep a minimum following distance of:
questions.explanation: More distance between your vehicle and others gives you more time to react. Keep at least two seconds of distance in normal conditions. Increase this distance in bad weather or heavy traffic.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street the wrong way.
Do not drive in this lane.
Left-turning traffic on a green light must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left-turning traffic on a green light must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign works with a traffic light to tell drivers turning left that they do not have the right-of-way. They must wait for oncoming traffic to pass before turning.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Always have the right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming toward you. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a vehicle that is close may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Turn the wheel too far in the opposite direction.
Turn your steering wheel into traffic.
Turn your steering wheel in the direction the vehicle is skidding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel in the direction the vehicle is skidding.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, stay calm. Steer the wheel in the same direction the skid is moving.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be prepared to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. You must stop completely if traffic requires it.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The overpass ahead has low clearance.
Two lanes of opposite traffic are about to merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The overpass ahead has low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the overpass ahead is low. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown (13 feet, 6 inches in this case).

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Turn right after making a complete stop.

questions.explanation: Regulatory signs show rules that drivers must follow. This sign means right turns are not permitted at this location.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway slants toward the left. This shows:

options.text: You must turn left just ahead.

questions.explanation: The solid line marks the edge of the road. When this line angles toward the center, it means the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: When you drive faster, what happens to your field of vision?

options.text: It makes it easier to see cross traffic.

questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the narrower your field of vision becomes. As speed increases, you see less of the road around you. You must stay alert to find hazards.

questions.question: An oncoming car is heading toward you in your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Honk, steer left, and slow down.
Honk, steer right, and slow down.
Stay in your lane, honk, and slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, steer right, and slow down.
questions.explanation: First, honk to get the other driver's attention. If they don't move, steer to the right to escape. Do not steer left because if the other driver swerves at the last moment, you will still crash. Slow down firmly and steadily. Every mile per hour you reduce your speed lowers the impact force.

questions.question: If your license was suspended before and reinstated, it will be suspended again if you get ____ points in three years.
questions.explanation: Driving violations add points to your record. If you get eight points against a previously suspended license, your license will be suspended again. A second suspension lasts six months. A third suspension lasts 12 months.

questions.question: What does a pennant-shaped sign mean?
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs warn of a no passing zone. This is the only use for this sign shape.

questions.question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this emblem drive 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: When you approach an intersection with no traffic light or stop sign, you should:

options.text: Keep going at the same speed.
Stop, look all around, then go.

questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to vehicles coming from the right. Always be prepared to yield to avoid a crash. Do this by easing off the gas, covering the brake, and looking left, right, and left again.

questions.question: When can you cross a solid yellow line?

options.text: To pass cars moving the same direction

questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed. Solid yellow lines cannot be crossed, except when you are turning.

questions.question: When visibility is reduced, what should you do first?
questions.explanation: Slowing down is your first action when you see reduced visibility or dangerous road conditions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic going the same direction will soon become one lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for traffic on your right.
Don't park on the right side.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash through a symbol means that action is not allowed. In this case, right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph needs up to ____ to stop completely.
questions.explanation: Heavy tractor-trailers need much longer distances to stop than smaller cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph may need almost 400 feet to stop completely.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a sharp right turn is coming up.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other:

options.text: It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
After one train passes, look for a second train on the other track before proceeding.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: After one train passes, look for a second train on the other track before proceeding.
questions.explanation: When two railroad tracks are next to each other, another train may be coming on the other track after the first train passes. Check both tracks before crossing. Do not cross until you are sure no train is approaching on either track.

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as a:
questions.explanation: A red flashing traffic light has the same meaning as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: If a vehicle using high beams comes toward you, you should look toward the ____ of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming vehicle's high beams are blinding you, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on your path until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Enter faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up to match traffic speed. Signal, look for an opening, accelerate, and merge safely into traffic.

questions.question: This sign warns drivers about:

options.text: A curve in the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A curve in the road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road curves to the right ahead.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a school crossing is ahead.

questions.question: Which of the following best keeps you and others safe when backing your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
Turn up the radio before backing up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Before getting in the driver's seat, walk to the back and check for children and small objects.

questions.question: If you are following a school bus or tank truck, you should:

options.text: Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: School buses and tank trucks carrying flammable materials must stop at railroad crossings. Be prepared to stop if you are following one of these vehicles.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that people may be crossing the road. Watch for pedestrians in the crosswalk. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What colors are highway exit distance signs?
questions.explanation: Destination signs are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: How should you treat railroad crossings?

options.text: Safe to cross, as trains rarely come.

questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Always look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs, signals, and flaggers. Only cross when you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: Your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Do not leave the scene without giving your information and offering help.

questions.question: Where should a pedestrian walk on a road with no sidewalk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side traffic is moving.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Walk on the side of the road facing the traffic nearest you. This lets you see cars coming toward you.

questions.question: To check your blind spot before turning left, look:
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot.

questions.question: How should drivers use the shared center lane on a multilane road?

options.text: To slow down or stop before turning left.
As a lane for through traffic when traffic is slow.

questions.correctAnswerText: To slow down or stop before turning left.
questions.explanation: Use the center lane only to slow down or stop for a safe left turn. Never use it to pass or as a through-traffic lane.
